omar: Quick Q — trying to find ingress log for trace ab12cd34ef and saw span with attribute http.request_id=req-77a. Trace Explorer shows spans but "Open related logs" missing. Where should I look via console/CLI?

maria: First checklist: open the span -> View raw span -> Attributes. Look for request.headers.x-request-id, x-b3-traceid, or http.request_id. If you have a pod name use stern/kubectl.

tony: Commands I usually run:

```
# follow pods by label and grep for either req id or trace id
stern -n prod "inference-api" --since 30m | rg "req-77a|ab12cd34ef"

# if you know the pod name
kubectl -n prod logs inference-api-6b9c -c inference | rg "req-77a"
```

Also check the edge proxy namespace — the proxy often rewrites the id.

lucy: Console tip: in Logs UI try this query exactly: `request_id:"req-77a" OR trace_id:"ab12cd34ef"`. Set time range +/- 5m around the span timestamp and group by pod. If Trace Explorer link is missing, use the span.service.name and span.timestamp to narrow the window.

devops-bot: Note: deploy-bot says prod log retention changed recently (infra 7d, edge-proxy 30d) — double-check time range.

omar: Found something — span had `edge.request_id=r-992` and downstream `http.request_id=req-77a`. Stern on edge namespace returned the ingress line. Thanks all. Filing a follow-up to add a trace->logs deep link that uses span attributes.

maria: Nice! For the follow-up, propose the Trace Explorer fallback builds a Logs UI query from span attributes (service, pod, request header keys). I'll sketch an RFC and tag @product and @eng-platform.
